=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer review

## Bottom line

The Seller’s package leaves Wattlebridge paying **AUD 24 million for substantially more risk than the debt-free/cash-free bargain suggests**. The most immediate completion risks are the unresolved Riverlark facility, the conditional Bluefen consent, and whether completion bonuses and other obligations are accounted for in the price. The proposed liability, disclosure and knowledge provisions would also make it unusually difficult to recover if a problem emerges.

The Seller’s update is a summary, not the complete SPA. The recommendations below should be checked against the full agreement, the underlying due diligence documents and the proposed funds flow.

## 1. Price, debt and completion funds flow

### Riverlark facility — require repayment and release at Completion

DD-003 records approximately **AUD 3.2 million outstanding** and a change-control provision. The facility has not been repaid and no final security discharge is included. A release after Completion would leave the Buyer owning a company with the debt and security still outstanding, contrary to the agreed debt-free/cash-free basis.

**Push back:** Make repayment and discharge a simultaneous Completion deliverable. Obtain a lender payout letter confirming the amount needed at Completion, payment instructions, release of all security and guarantees, and any necessary change-of-control waiver or consent. The funds flow should pay the lender directly from amounts otherwise payable to the Seller, with effective releases delivered at Completion or a tightly controlled, enforceable discharge process. Confirm treatment of accrued interest, break costs and fees. The Buyer should not pay the full price to the Seller and then fund the debt again.

### Completion bonuses — resolve the economic burden expressly

DD-005 records **AUD 420,000** of conditional bonuses, but they are absent from the funds flow. The Seller’s assertion that they are its matter does not establish who will pay them or bear associated payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs. The continued-employment conditions also mean the ultimate amount and timing need verification.

**Push back:** Require an employee-by-employee schedule, payment and on-cost calculation, and an express allocation to the Seller to the extent arising from the transaction or pre-Completion arrangements. Provide for payment or an appropriate price adjustment, retention or indemnity, including amounts that become payable after Completion because the conditions are later satisfied. Avoid double counting under the purchase-price mechanics.

### Supplier renewals — do not accept their categorisation without evidence

The three Sandbar renewals total **AUD 330,000**, but the disclosure does not establish whether they are accrued, unavoidable, terminable or ordinary-course costs. They are not automatically debt merely because they are identified in due diligence.

**Push back:** Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and obtain the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights and any unpaid or accrued amounts. Allocate any pre-Completion liabilities or exceptional, transaction-driven commitments through the agreed price mechanics or a specific protection; ordinary post-Completion operating costs should be assessed on their merits. Check the adjustment mechanism for omissions and double counting.

## 2. Conditions and key commercial relationships

### Bluefen — consent must be effective, not merely delivered

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, or 30%**. No final consent or evidence that its associated conditions are satisfied has been provided. Treating the condition as satisfied merely upon delivery of a written consent risks accepting a conditional, ineffective or commercially damaging consent.

**Push back:** Require, as a condition to Completion, a final written consent effective for the transaction, with the requirements of clauses 11.2 and 11.3 satisfied or validly waived. It should not introduce unacceptable amendments or obligations. Strengthen the Seller’s obligation to pursue it, require prompt disclosure of correspondence and give the Buyer approval over material proposed terms. Include a workable long-stop and consequences if the condition is not satisfied; do not waive it without a separate commercial assessment.

### Office lease and Mossvale — verify, but do not overstate

DD-007 identifies a **notification**, not a landlord consent requirement. DD-009 identifies an **assignment restriction**, not a stated share-sale consent requirement.

**Push back:** Confirm the underlying provisions and ensure any required lease notice is given on time. Check whether the proposed transaction involves an assignment or any other trigger under Mossvale, but do not demand a consent solely on the facts currently disclosed.

## 3. Liability and remedies

### General cap, thresholds and time limit

The Seller proposes a **AUD 4.8 million cap** on general warranty claims, a **AUD 25,000 per-claim threshold**, a **AUD 250,000 excess-only basket**, and an **18-month notification period**. Together, these materially reduce the practical value of the warranties: even after qualifying claims exceed the basket, the first AUD 250,000 remains with the Buyer.

**Push back:** Seek a higher general cap, a lower de minimis, a *tipping* basket under which qualifying losses are recoverable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded, and a longer claim-notification period. At minimum, ensure related claims can be aggregated and that notification need only provide reasonable available detail, with later updates permitted. These are negotiation positions; their final levels should reflect diligence, insurance and the commercial risk allocation.

### Fundamental warranties and tax need separate protection

Applying the general cap and 18-month period to **title and capacity** is not acceptable: defects could affect the Buyer’s ownership of the entire business. The Seller also places tax and IP under the general regime, although tax exposures can emerge well after 18 months and core IP may be central to the business’s value.

**Push back:**

- Separate fundamental warranties—including title, ownership, capacity and authority—from the general regime. Seek a cap of at least the purchase price and a longer survival period aligned with the applicable limitation period.
- Seek a standalone pre-Completion tax covenant or indemnity, with a suitable cap and period reflecting relevant assessment and amendment periods.
- Assess whether core IP ownership warranties warrant enhanced protection; deal with the identified Ironquay risk separately.
- Make explicit which limitations apply to each category, rather than relying on the Seller’s proposed default that all limitations apply to all claims.

### Fraud, exclusive remedy and non-reliance

Clauses described as applying limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to **all claims of any nature** could restrict remedies even for serious misconduct or claims under specific protections.

**Push back:** Expressly preserve claims for fraud and deliberate misconduct, and ensure caps, thresholds and time limits do not apply to those claims. Preserve the intended operation of specific indemnities, the tax covenant, price-adjustment and completion-payment obligations, and equitable or other remedies where appropriate. Review the actual wording and interaction of clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5; the legal effect of any exclusion will depend on that wording and applicable law.

## 4. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

### Data-room and public-records blanket disclosure

The Seller seeks to disclose everything in the data room, accounts, registers and public records. This could turn a large volume of documents into a broad defence, whether or not a specific risk is readily identifiable. The Buyer-knowledge clause goes further by excluding matters merely **discoverable** by the Buyer or its advisers.

**Push back:** Require disclosure to be **fairly disclosed**: sufficiently clear and detailed to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its relevance to the relevant warranty. Reject blanket public-record and data-room disclosure as an automatic qualification. Limit any knowledge exclusion to the actual knowledge of specifically named Buyer personnel, not constructive knowledge or everything advisers could have discovered. Neither disclosure nor knowledge should defeat expressly negotiated specific protections.

The specific disclosures do, however, identify real matters that need active treatment. Narrowing disclosure wording alone is not a substitute for resolving Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses and the incident.

## 5. Identified specific risks

### Ironquay IP — broaden beyond the SOW3 payment

DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 records **AUD 180,000 open**, but does not independently prove non-payment; there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. An indemnity limited to that specific payment may not cover an ownership defect, other unpaid fees or the consequences of an IP dispute.

**Push back:** Before Completion, verify all SOW3 fees and obtain evidence of cleared payment plus a direct, effective confirmatory assignment or acknowledgement covering the relevant Project Materials and chain of title. Require a broader specific indemnity for losses arising from the identified payment, ownership and rights issue, including reasonable defence and remediation costs. Consider a retention if the position cannot be resolved before Completion.

### Export/privacy incident — investigate without assuming a breach

DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external email address; the export **may** contain approximately **1,240 records**. Access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unestablished. The Seller’s “preliminary” characterisation is not a resolution, but the current facts do not establish a confirmed breach either.

**Push back:** Obtain the investigation, access and audit logs, containment steps, affected-data assessment and advice on applicable notification obligations. Require the Seller to preserve evidence and cooperate with the Buyer. Seek a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related losses and reasonable investigation, notification and remediation costs, appropriately addressing any recovery from third parties. Consider retention or another targeted protection if the investigation remains open at signing or Completion.

### Share title — register is evidence, not the whole protection

DD-012 records the Seller as holder of 100% of the issued shares. That is useful evidence, but it does not by itself establish that all shares are free from encumbrances or that all transfer requirements will be met.

**Push back:** Verify the capitalisation and share register against the constitution and relevant corporate records; check for options, rights and encumbrances. Require title and capacity warranties and Completion deliverables including properly executed transfers, share certificates where applicable, and necessary corporate approvals and releases. Ensure the Buyer receives the documents needed to be registered as holder of all issued shares.

## Recommended negotiating priorities

1. **Do not complete with Riverlark outstanding:** agree direct repayment, releases and a verified funds flow consistent with the debt-free/cash-free price.
2. **Make Bluefen an effective, unconditional-or-satisfied consent condition**, not simply a document-delivery condition.
3. **Allocate the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs**, and investigate the Sandbar renewals before fixing the completion calculation.
4. **Ring-fence title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud/deliberate misconduct** from the general limitations; improve the general cap, basket, threshold and time limit.
5. **Reject blanket disclosure and discoverable-knowledge exclusions**; require fair disclosure and a narrow actual-knowledge standard.
6. **Resolve or specifically protect Ironquay and the export incident**, with evidence and targeted indemnities or retention where necessary.
7. **Complete title and contract-trigger verification**, without treating the office lease or Mossvale as requiring consent absent supporting wording.
